I've been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for twenty years now, and I know this land well. My husband works off-farm at a factory in Handan, so it's mostly me making the day-to-day decisions, though he comes back to help at harvest and planting. With only two of us, I can't afford to waste labor or money on things that don't pay back.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant the whole 8 mu right after the National Day holiday in early October. I always use the improved Jinmai or Shixin varieties that the seed shop sells — they yield better than the old traditional wheat and stand up to the cold Hebei winter. Before planting, I'll plough the field to bury the maize stalks from the summer crop and break up the soil. I'll put down compound fertilizer as my base dressing, then topdress with urea at green-up time and again at jointing. I know this soil is reasonably fertile, but twenty years of wheat-maize rotation has taught me it needs feeding. I'll irrigate three times from the well: once before winter to help the seedlings establish, once at jointing in spring when the wheat is shooting up, and once at grain filling in May. Three times is enough — electricity for the well pump costs money, and over-watering just makes the plants lodge. I'll spray herbicide after the first irrigation in spring, and maybe one fungicide if I see rust starting. I'm expecting around 500 jin per mu if the spring weather cooperates.

For the summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off the thresher in early June, I'll get the hybrid seed in the ground. You have to be quick — the growing season is tight before autumn frost. I use rotary tillage after wheat harvest to save time and keep some residue cover, then plant. Maize needs nitrogen, so I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea when the plants are knee-high. I'll irrigate twice — once when the tassels are coming out and once during grain filling if the July rains don't come. The monsoon usually helps, but you can't count on it. Two pesticide sprays: a pre-emergence herbicide and one insecticide for corn borer around the big喇叭口 stage. With good management, I should get about 600 jin per mu from the maize.
